summary: The download page offers Windows and Linux choices from actual published release assets, while macOS remains unavailable until its build is repaired. New normal releases contain Bunzai.exe, Bunzai-Linux for x64, and SHA256SUMS. Both apps include the remote helper; preparation never enables mesh access. Linux no-argument launch starts Studio and opens the browser after the file is made executable. Older Linux CLI files require the ui command. Existing helper and CLI release files remain for recovery. Advanced automation and ARM64 users can run or build from source. The guide covers pinned Bun, recursive RP-Core checkout, setup, providers, encrypted-library backups, source updates and startup troubleshooting. Browser Studio is temporary and Kit remains source-only.

sections.title: What is available today
sections.summary: Use the download page to select Windows or Linux from actual GitHub assets; macOS is marked unavailable until repaired. New normal releases publish Bunzai.exe, Bunzai-Linux for x64 and SHA256SUMS. The checksum list verifies the apps, while automatic source archives are for development. Open the Windows executable directly. On Linux, chmod the file executable and run it without arguments to start Studio and open the browser; keep its terminal open. Older bunzai-cli-linux-x64 files need the ui command. New apps include their helper and prepare a verified copy without another download or enabling remote access. Old helper files stay on prior releases for recovery. Updating source does not add bundled bytes to an older installed executable. Browser Studio loses tab data on reload; Kit is source-only.

sections.title: Run from source
sections.summary: This checkout pins Bun 1.4.2. Install Bun using its official platform instructions, open a new terminal, and confirm the version with bun --version. Clone the repository with --recurse-submodules so the pinned RP-Core dependency is present, then run bun install --frozen-lockfile and bun run dev. The server normally binds to 127.0.0.1:8321 and prints the address it actually uses. If that port is occupied, it checks nearby local ports. Leave the terminal open while using the Studio and press Ctrl+C when finished.

children.title: Advanced: CLI and Linux ARM64
children.summary: Automation and bulk conversion use CLI commands from a source checkout, with help available through bun run src/cli.ts help. ARM64 devices can use the same source workflow. Compiling a Linux ARM64 executable requires Go to build the matching helper with sidecar/build.ts, followed by build-desktop.ts with no desktop and the bun-linux-arm64 CLI target. The resulting dist/bunzai-cli-linux-arm64 starts Studio with its ui command. Ordinary users do not need that extra build or the internal Windows CLI used for release verification.

sections.title: First launch
sections.summary: A new studio folder opens the first-run wizard, which asks about appearance, the kinds of pieces you use, publish targets, and accent color. You can skip it; the choices can be changed later in Settings. After setup, use the Library to import a supported file or start a blank character. Importing, editing, and converting local files do not require a provider connection. To generate a scene reply, configure a provider connection and select an available model. A submitted turn sends its assembled request to that provider, and any account or usage charges come from the provider.

sections.title: Your library and recovery
sections.summary: The installed Studio keeps an encrypted SQLite library named library.db inside its studio folder. Unless you choose another folder, it is Documents/Bunzai Studio in your user profile; the server prints the full path at startup. Before moving the folder or updating source, create a protected backup through Settings > Backups. A folder copy contains the database and snapshots, but opening it may also require the password or recovery words and the computer's local key material. Keep recovery words somewhere separate. The checkout and studio folder are separate; removing the checkout does not remove library data.

sections.title: Update a source checkout
sections.summary: Stop the running server with Ctrl+C before updating. From the checkout, use git pull --ff-only, git submodule update --init --recursive, bun install --frozen-lockfile, and bun run dev. This keeps the pinned submodule and lockfile dependencies in step with the updated source. Back up the library first if it matters to you; updating the checkout does not itself change the studio folder. If Git reports local changes or cannot fast-forward, review them before proceeding. Do not force a reset over work you have not inspected.

sections.title: If something does not open
sections.summary: Check Bun against the checkout's 1.4.2 pin and use official installation or upgrade instructions. Missing RP-Core requires recursive submodule initialization and a frozen-lockfile install. Open the exact local address printed by the running server. Windows desktop apps require WebView2, documented by Microsoft's distribution and download pages. Release binaries must match the operating system and architecture and the release's checksum; workflow platform names do not create unpublished assets. Current supported app builds include the remote helper. Older builds and source checkouts may use the verified download offered in Settings. A preparation failure leaves ordinary local Studio use available. Preparing or downloading the helper does not enable remote access.

sections.title: Related guides
sections.summary: For a shorter first-run walkthrough, continue to Get started. Troubleshooting covers common local problems and the Studio reference describes the local application and API. The links use the same bundled Docs pages so you can navigate between them without leaving the site. If you are deciding whether to use the source checkout or a future packaged version, check the availability statement at the top of this page first.
